newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JULY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JULY 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Gencor Ltd chairman Brian Gilbertson said on Tuesday privatisation of South American mines would be a major focus of Billiton Plc once it was listed in London, and indications were that the share offer would raise substantially more than the one billion pounds sterling originally envisaged.

- The South African Chamber of Business launched a fresh attack on the government's industrial offset programme, saying it contravened World Trade Organisation rules and was an unnecessary intervention in the tendering system.
- The rand breached the key 4.55 rand to the dollar level and weakened nearly two cents on the ailing gold price, even though the metal showed some improvement on Tuesday.

- The gold mining industry could shed as many as 100,000 jobs at marginal gold mines if the bullion price continues its weak trend, according to analysts and economists. This further dampened hopes that the government's job-creation targets would be reached. The Chamber of Mines said it did not expect the government to help the struggling industry.

- South African Breweries Ltd's beer division will submit a new proposal for the establishment of a 100 million rand brewery in Namibia next month, said Andre Parker, managing director of the African division of SAB international. SAB's attempts to set up an operation in Namibia have twice been thwarted by the Namibian government.

- Commercial banks said they were fiercely opposed to a recommendation by the Reserve Bank to Finance Minister Trevor Manuel that they be forced to sell deposit insurance to clients placing amounts smaller than 30,000 rand. Customers would pay for the insurance by accepting lower interest rates on their deposits, according to the proposal.

- Insecurity over the lower gold price on Tuesday pressured the rand which saw the South African currency weaken against the dollar to its lowest level in five months. Dealers said strong demand for dollars was prompted by fears that thousands of jobs could be lost if marginal mines were closed, coupled with the decline in the value of South Africa's gold reserves.

- The South African Chamber of Business' confidence index rose by 0.8 percentage points to 114.6 points in June from 113.8 points the previous month. The moderate improvement was attributed in part to forecasts of lower interest rates in the second half of the year.
- SMX, the mining explosives division of South Africa's Sasol Ltd , has taken an equity stake in U.S.-based DHB Holdings Inc, the two groups said in a statement.

- The middle-aged parents of U.S. exchange student Amy Biehl, who was murdered in Cape Town's Guguletu township in 1993, spent five hours on Tuesday watching as three of the men who stoned and stabbed their daughter to death described the attack. All three, who are hoping to be granted amnesty, were members of the Pan Africanist Congress.

- The National Party's former rising star Roelf Meyer and former renegade African National Congress MP Bantu Holomisa, on Tuesday announced they would join forces to form a new political party on September 27.
